correctness.rationale: Complete derivation: algebra/graph criteria (arXiv:1601.01832), exact GL block-upper-triangular and block-diagonal counts, unique connected-component recursion, Bonferroni singleton intersection bounds and exponentially smaller non-singleton cuts. All quantifiers are fixed-q, n to infinity. Exhaustive packaged checks include 20160 invertible binary 4-by-4 matrices. No finite test substitutes for the all-n proof.

originality.rationale: The evaluated contribution is the sharp pair of GL-conditioned support-connectivity probability laws with different exponential scales and their ratio, not the credited graph criteria or generic labelled exponential formula. The October 2026 primary survey explicitly identifies the problem class, and the original decomposition paper proves only structural graph equivalences. Specific literature and mathematical-record queries did not reveal these conditioned laws. A broader support-pattern enumeration may implicitly cover them and remains a stated risk.
residual_risks: A general enumeration of invertible matrices with prescribed support patterns could already imply this probability law, possibly in differently titled combinatorics literature.
Only the abstract was inspected for the earlier graph paper and the random-matrix rank paper; no claim of their full-document noncoverage is made.
Search nonhits are not proof of historical uniqueness.

value.rationale: An explicit question in the October 2026 survey asks for asymptotic probabilities of random simple and indecomposable evolution algebras. In the natural perfect dense model this theorem gives sharp leading constants and shows the decomposability probability is exponentially smaller than the nonsimplicity probability; an exact labelled recurrence gives finite-dimensional enumeration. These precise structural probabilities are motivated independently of the computational examples.
